clue.text: Musician's book is lacking support

indicators.note: the musician is lacking something, so one letter is taken away from the player's name

parts.note: a bassist is a musician who plays the bass guitar or double bass

explanation.surface: A musician's songbook has gone missing and he needs some backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Musician's book is lacking' as 'the musician is lacking book': BASSIST loses its B.
explanation.definitionFit: To support someone is to help or back them, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Fact: if swimming round lake, that's trouble

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for lake
letters that are swimming move about freely and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Fact: if you go swimming round a lake you're in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges the fodder into AFFICT, and 'round' then places the lake's letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To afflict is to cause pain or distress, the verb sense of trouble.

clue.text: Short cut round T-bar

indicators.note: the shortened pieces go round the letter T

parts.note: S stands for short, as in clothing sizes and short-wave
to rip is to cut or tear
the letter T as printed in T-bar

explanation.surface: A quick way round a ski lift's T-bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip is a long narrow piece, like a bar of metal.

clue.text: Castrati failed to comprehend Latin composer

indicators.note: to comprehend is to take in, so the letters enclose the abbreviation
the singers failed, falling apart, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Castrato singers couldn't understand a composer who wrote in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' rearranges CASTRATI into SCARATTI; 'to comprehend' puts L inside. Domenico Scarlatti was an Italian baroque composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlatti was an Italian baroque composer, so the name is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Advanced because fighting Germany

parts.note: for can mean because, as in 'for he was tired'
fighting between nations is war
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: An army pushed on into new territory because it was at war with Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced and forward both describe something ahead of others or pushed ahead, as in a forward child.

clue.text: Sweet, affectionate article on collection of books

parts.note: fond means loving or affectionate
a is the indefinite article
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A sweet, loving piece written about a library collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft sugary paste used in sweets and icing.

clue.text: Meeting different sorts of people

definitions.meaning: a race meeting is an event of several horse ..., so the ... are the meeting

explanation.surface: A gathering of all kinds of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Races are a day's horse racing and also groups of humankind by ancestry.

clue.text: Jocular, mad, illogical centre for protected species

indicators.note: the answer sits at the centre of the three words, held within them

explanation.surface: A silly, crazy, nonsensical heart of a conservation programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span jocul-AR MAD ILLO-gical.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is protected by its bony armour plating, a playful sense of protected.

clue.text: To get unengaged, the chap had to take Kitty back

indicators.note: the whole is read back to front
the man's contraction takes in the cat, holding it inside

parts.note: the chap had is he'd, written HED
kitty is a pet name for a cat

explanation.surface: To break off his engagement, the fellow had to take the cat back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' gives HCATED, and 'back' reverses that whole string; he'd loses its apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach is to disconnect or separate, so something detached is no longer engaged or connected.

clue.text: Spanish artist admits resistance against reverse driving aid

indicators.note: against means next to, so the letters sit side by side
the painter admits, lets in, the letter for resistance

parts.note: Joan Miró was a Spanish surrealist painter
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
R is reverse on a car's gear stick

explanation.surface: A Spanish painter shows resistance to a reversing aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear-view mirror is a driving aid that lets the driver see behind.

clue.text: Data not in for Red Arrows display?

indicators.note: the data are to be taken without the word 'in', so those two letters are removed

parts.note: data are facts or information

explanation.surface: Someone asks for figures that weren't supplied for an air show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Arrows are the RAF's aerobatic display team, famous for flying in tight patterns; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Arrows fly in close formation, so a formation is an example of their display.

clue.text: Long-distance traveller needs to reach Everest's base

parts.note: to reach a place is to come to it

indicators.note: the base of a word is its final letter, here the last letter of the mountain's name

explanation.surface: A long-distance trekker must make it to Everest base camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet travels vast distances around the sun on its long orbit, a whimsical way to describe it.

clue.text: One's exercise at 50? Get going!

parts.note: 'one is', said as 'I am', contracts to I'M
PE is physical education, school exercise
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone turning fifty is told to start exercising and get a move on.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge forward, which is what a command to get going does.

clue.text: Effusive, improvised C sharp setting for Groom's Vow Rejected

indicators.note: the rearranged note acts as a setting for the vow, which sits inside it
music that is improvised is made up freshly, so the letters of the note are rearranged
the vow is turned back, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a groom's wedding vow is 'I do'

explanation.surface: A wedding song with an ad-libbed C sharp is the gushing setting for the groom's vow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improvised' rearranges C SHARP into RHAPSC; 'Rejected' turns I DO into ODI, which 'setting for' places inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsodic means gushing with enthusiasm, a close synonym of effusive.

clue.text: Barperson who has a sip (about a pint)

indicators.note: the sipper goes around the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: a taster is someone who takes a small sip to try something
P is an abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: A barman who sips the beer, here about a pint of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster is an old word for someone who draws beer in a bar.

clue.text: Sales publicity for poet?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
Andrew Motion was Britain's Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009

explanation.surface: Is there any marketing for poetry?
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Motion was the UK's Poet Laureate; being 'for' him is backing him.
explanation.definitionFit: Sales promotion is advertising and publicity meant to boost sales.

clue.text: Caught in lie about old advocate's outfit

indicators.note: the lawyer is caught in the story, held inside it

parts.note: a tale is a lie, as in 'telling tales'

indicators.note: the lawyer's abbreviation is turned around

parts.note: a KC, King's Counsel, is a senior barrister in Britain; 'old' as the title switches between QC and KC by monarch

explanation.surface: A lawyer's clothing gets caught up in a lie about an elderly barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: King's Counsel is a senior British barrister; 'about' turns its abbreviation round, and the grammar has the lie doing the catching.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is equipment or gear, as in fishing tackle, so it means an outfit.

clue.text: Who thinks Rocky too tragic?

indicators.note: rocky means shaky and unstable, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Who thinks the Rocky films are too tragic?
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to ponder deeply, so a cogitator is a person who thinks.

clue.text: Speaker's position, bottom of heap — shame

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: odium is disgrace or shame attached to someone

explanation.surface: A speaker at the bottom of the heap, in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is the raised platform where a speaker stands.

clue.text: Avoid stage production broadcast: it might infringe the rules

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so what is heard counts, not the spelling

parts.note: to avoid something is to miss it; a play is a production on stage

explanation.surface: Steer clear of the play being broadcast on air: it might break the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A misplay is a wrong or illegal move in a game, which can be a foul.

clue.text: Weed brings illness and bereavement

parts.note: a bug is a minor illness, like a stomach bug
bereavement is the loss of a loved one

explanation.surface: Some weed brings sickness and grief.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugloss is a bristly plant of the borage family, often treated as a weed.

clue.text: Rogue commanded galleons originally

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to command
each galleon's original letter is G, and for plural galleons it is doubled, the way PP stands for pages

explanation.surface: A pirate captain gave orders to his fleet of galleons.
explanation.walkthrough: Because galleons is plural, its opening letter is taken twice, one for each ship, as abbreviations double for plurals (pp for pages).
explanation.definitionFit: A bad egg is an idiom for a rogue, a person of bad character.

clue.text: Second one to cry "Besom"?

parts.note: a weeper is one who weeps or cries

explanation.surface: Another person ready to burst into tears calls out a strange word.
explanation.definitionFit: A besom is a broom made of twigs, and a sweeper is a broom or brush.

clue.text: Pound no good — raise

parts.note: duff is British slang for useless or no good
to up something is to raise it, as in upping the price

explanation.surface: The pound is worthless, so put up prices.
explanation.walkthrough: DUFF is British slang for useless; DUFF UP is British slang for beat someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To duff up is slang for to beat or pound someone.

clue.text: Lacking competition, large organisation sat after work

indicators.note: the word for sat is placed after the word for work

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is a large international organisation
op is short for opus, a work
to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat is posed

explanation.surface: A large body faced no rivals after its staff sat down at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Unopposed means without any challenger or rival standing against you.

clue.text: Feature of flower power: raised behind

parts.note: P is the symbol for power

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: A hippie's flower power slogan is late to the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is part of a flower's corolla, a distinctive feature of blooms.

clue.text: Submit pill when temperature's taken

indicators.note: the temperature is taken away, so its letter is removed

parts.note: a tablet is a pill
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Someone told to swallow a pill while having their temperature taken.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage to table a motion is to submit it for discussion.

clue.text: Sands (new for start of athletics) settle

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another, so it is replaced

parts.note: the sands are the beach

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Sands, where a new start in athletics might settle.
explanation.walkthrough: In BEACH the A, start of 'athletics', is replaced by N for new.
explanation.definitionFit: A settle is a high-backed wooden bench, a crossword favourite sense.

clue.text: Feature of fencing's noisy collapse

indicators.note: a noisy version is one that is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to faint is to collapse

explanation.surface: A fence's loud collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A feint is a pretended attack used in fencing to mislead an opponent.

clue.text: Turn the screw left not right ultimately, to relax?

indicators.note: left comes in instead of the other letter, which is not used

parts.note: to turn the screw is to tighten up, increasing pressure

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word right

explanation.surface: Instructions for turning a screw left rather than right to loosen it.
explanation.walkthrough: In TIGHTEN UP, the T (end of 'right') is swapped for L (left); the question mark admits that loosening up is the opposite of the screw image.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighten up is an idiom meaning relax and stop being so serious.

clue.text: Play ten rounds as punishment

indicators.note: the letters go round and round, being shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A boxer made to fight ten rounds as a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A penalty is a punishment imposed for breaking a rule.

clue.text: Who might pierce inner ear, being vexed about Queen and Church

indicators.note: the mixed letters wrap around the abbreviations for queen and church
vexed means troubled or stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: R is short for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: Someone who would pierce the inner ear, upset about the Queen and the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vexed' gives AER, and 'about' wraps it round the two abbreviations after its A. The inner is a ring on an archery target, near the bullseye.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer aims arrows at a target, whose inner ring an arrow might pierce.
